title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
authors: S. Borgeaud, A. Mensch, J. Hoffmann, et al. (28 authors)
before: Retrieval was bolted on at inference time to a model trained without it.
problem: If a model can look things up, it should not have to memorise them in its weights.
breakthrough: Retrieve from a two-trillion-token database during pretraining itself, via chunked cross-attention.
why: It showed a 7B model with retrieval matching much larger ones, arguing memory and reasoning can be separated.
next: The idea recurs in long-context and memory work, though frontier labs largely chose bigger contexts instead.
inherits: The open question of what belongs in weights versus in an external store.
